device-missing.mic: Your microphone is no longer connected. Plug it back in (or reconnect the Bluetooth headset): the app reconnects by itself. If you now use a different mic, select it in Settings → Devices.
device-missing.toCall: CABLE-A Input (the virtual cable that carries your voice to the call) has disappeared. Reinstall or re-enable VB-CABLE A+B, restart the PC, then press Re-detect in Settings → VB-CABLE A · B.
device-missing.fromCall: CABLE-B Output (the virtual cable that brings the call into the app) has disappeared. Reinstall or re-enable VB-CABLE A+B, restart the PC, then press Re-detect in Settings → VB-CABLE A · B.
device-missing.headset: Your headset or speakers are no longer connected. Plug them back in: the app reconnects by itself. If you now use a different device, select it in Settings → Devices.

device-failed.mic: The app can't open your microphone. Close other apps that may be holding it and check Windows Settings → Privacy & security → Microphone (allow desktop apps). The app retries by itself; if it doesn't recover, unplug and replug the mic, or stop and restart the translation if it is running.
device-failed.toCall: The app can't play into CABLE-A Input. In Windows Sound settings check that the cable is enabled. The app retries by itself; if it doesn't recover, stop and restart the translation (if it is running) or restart the PC.
device-failed.fromCall: The app can't record from CABLE-B Output. In Windows Sound settings → Recording check that it is enabled and not used exclusively by another app. The app retries by itself; if it doesn't recover, stop and restart the translation (if it is running) or restart the PC.
device-failed.headset: The app can't play on your headset. Check that it is on and connected (unplug and replug it), or select it again in Settings → Devices. The app retries by itself; if it doesn't recover, stop and restart the translation if it is running.

fix.mic-silent: Your microphone has sent only complete silence since the translation started: it may be muted. Unmute it (headset mute button, keyboard mic key, or Windows Settings → Sound → Input volume) and check that the right mic is selected in Settings → Devices. If you just haven't spoken yet, ignore this: it disappears as soon as you talk.
fix.call-silent: Nothing has arrived from the call app since the translation started. In the audio settings of Meet, Teams or Zoom set Speakers to "{{speaker}}". Also check that the meeting tab isn't muted. If the other person simply hasn't spoken yet, this disappears as soon as they do.
fix.audio-suspended: Windows paused the app's audio (often after sleep or a device change). The app tries to resume it by itself; if it doesn't, stop and restart the translation (if it is running), or quit and reopen the app.
fix.mic-quiet: Your voice reaches the app, but too quietly to be translated. Raise the microphone input volume in Windows Settings → Sound → Input (70–100%), move closer to the mic, and check that the right mic is selected in Settings → Devices.
fix.call-quiet: The call's audio reaches the app, but too quietly to be translated. Set the call app's volume to 100% (and Chrome/Edge or the call app in the Windows Volume mixer), and set the level of CABLE-B Input to 100% in Windows Sound settings → Playback → Properties → Levels.

trouble.heading: Troubleshooting
trouble.sub: If something doesn't work, start here: run the audio check, read the problems detected right now and follow the guide for your call app.

check.heading: Audio check
check.intro: Checks every device and both virtual cables in a few seconds. The translation must be stopped. Note: a short, quiet test tone is sent into the call through CABLE-A and another one plays in your headset — if you are in a meeting, mute yourself in the call app first.
check.during: During the check: speak into your mic, and in the call app press 'Test speakers' (or let the other person talk).
check.busy: Stop the translation first (■ button on the bar), then run the check again.
check.failed: The check could not run: {{message}}. Close this window, reopen Troubleshooting and try again.
check.allPass: Everything works. If the other person still can't hear you, check the call app settings in the guides below.
check.skippedHint: Not run: an earlier check failed or a setting is missing.

api-key.fix: No OpenAI key is saved. Open Settings → OpenAI API Key and paste your key (it starts with sk-).

devices-saved.fix: Not all four devices are selected. Open Settings → Devices and choose microphone, output to call, capture from call and headset.

mic-present.title: Microphone connected
mic-present.fix: The selected microphone isn't connected. Plug it in, or choose another one in Settings → Devices.

mic-signal.title: Your voice reaches the app
mic-signal.fix: Your mic is silent or too quiet for the translation. Speak during the check, unmute the mic, raise the input volume in Windows Settings → Sound → Input (70–100%), and make sure the right mic is selected in Settings → Devices.

to-call-present.title: CABLE-A Input present
to-call-present.fix: CABLE-A Input is missing. Install VB-CABLE A+B, restart the PC, then choose CABLE-A Input as 'Output to call' in Settings → Devices.

cable-a-loopback.title: CABLE-A carries your voice to the call
cable-a-loopback.fix: A test sound played into CABLE-A Input didn't come out of CABLE-A Output. In Windows Sound settings → Recording, enable CABLE-A Output and make sure it isn't muted; set all CABLE devices to 48000 Hz; restart the PC if needed.

from-call-present.title: CABLE-B Output present
from-call-present.fix: CABLE-B Output is missing. Install VB-CABLE A+B, restart the PC, then choose CABLE-B Output as 'Capture from call' in Settings → Devices.

call-signal.title: Sound from the call app arrives
call-signal.fix: No sound, or too little, arrived from the call app. In the call app set Speakers to "{{speaker}}" and its volume to 100%; in the Windows Volume mixer set Chrome/Edge (or the call app) to 100%, and in Windows Sound settings → Playback set the level of CABLE-B Input to 100%. Then run the check again and press 'Test speakers' (or let the other person talk) while it runs.

headset-present.title: Headset connected
headset-present.fix: The selected headset isn't connected. Plug it in or turn it on, or choose another one in Settings → Devices.

headset-tone.title: Test tone on your headset
headset-tone.fix: The test tone couldn't be played on your headset. Check it is on and connected, raise the volume, and select it again in Settings → Devices.

guides.heading: Step-by-step guides
guides.devicesIntro: These are the exact names to select in your call app:

meet.title: Google Meet (Chrome / Edge)
meet.step1: In the meeting, click ⋮ (More options) → Settings → Audio.
meet.step4: Turn OFF "Noise cancellation" and "Adaptive audio": they treat the translated voice as noise and cut it.
meet.step5: Make sure the Meet tab isn't muted (right-click the tab) and that the site may use the microphone (lock icon in the address bar → Microphone: Allow).
meet.step6: Check these settings again after every browser restart: Chrome and Edge may go back to "Default" on their own.

teams.title: Microsoft Teams
teams.step1: Open Settings (… next to your profile picture) → Devices → Audio devices and choose "Custom setup".
teams.step5: During a meeting, check under … → Settings → Device settings that the same devices are still selected.

zoom.title: Zoom
zoom.step5: Background noise suppression: Low or Off — or enable "Original sound for musicians" and turn it on in the meeting.

windows.title: Windows sound settings
windows.step1: Never set a CABLE device as the Windows default or default communication device: your real mic and headset must stay the defaults.
windows.step2: Sound control panel → Communications tab → choose "Do nothing", so Windows doesn't lower the volume during calls.
windows.step3: All CABLE devices (Playback and Recording tabs) must use the same format: Properties → Advanced → 48000 Hz.
windows.step4: In the same Advanced tab, uncheck "Allow applications to take exclusive control of this device" for every CABLE device.
windows.step5: Bluetooth headsets: prefer a wired or USB headset. With Bluetooth, select the "Hands-Free" devices for both mic and headset.
windows.step6: If the audio crackles or stutters: open the VB-CABLE control panel and raise "Max Latency".

phantom.q: I hear phrases like "I'm ready, let's talk" that nobody said
phantom.a: The translator received only silence and made up a sentence. The call app isn't sending audio to CABLE-B: set its Speakers to "{{speaker}}" and run the audio check.

notHeard.q: Nobody hears me (or they hear me cut off)
notHeard.a: The call app's microphone isn't "{{mic}}", or its noise cancellation is removing the translated voice. Fix the microphone in the call app and turn noise cancellation off.

echo.q: The other person hears an echo
echo.a: The sound from your speakers goes back into your mic. Use headphones instead of speakers and keep the volume moderate.

direct.q: Before I press play, I hear the call untranslated
direct.a: That's direct mode, and it's intended: while translation is off the app passes your voice and the call through unchanged, so you're never left without audio. Press ▶ on the bar to translate. If nobody has talked on either side for 10 minutes, the app releases your microphone (Bluetooth headsets go back to full quality) and reopens it as soon as sound arrives from the call.
